title: Quiz Demo
text:
Q1. Match each description with the corresponding R function featured in this chapter.



Returns a quantile of a normally distributed random variable:  Choose… dbinom() pbinom() pnorm() qnorm() pnorm() prop.table() 


Calculates the probability of a binomial random variable X being at most a specified value:  Choose… dbinom() pbinom() pnorm() qnorm() pnorm() prop.table() 


Validates the estimated probabilities described in the Empirical Rule:  Choose… dbinom() pbinom() pnorm() qnorm() pnorm() prop.table() 






Q2. If the chance that it will snow today is 13%, then by the  Choose… addition delulu multiplication negation three-month rizz  rule, the probability it will not is 87%.





Q3. Let’s say an airline sold tickets to 140 people, each of whom will either show up to fly or will not show up to fly. They have observed historically a 9% probability that a passenger will be a no-show for a flight. They issued 140 tickets for 134 seats because they expect at least 6 no-shows. Assume each passenger showing up or not showing up to fly are independent. What is the probability that there are fewer than 6 no-shows?



  0.7% 


  1.1% 


  1.6% 


  2.7% 


  97% 


  99%
